title: Python decompiler version coverage
subtitle: declared bytecode ranges; recovery quality and verification differ by tool
note: Bars summarize upstream bytecode-version claims checked on 2026-09-09, not accuracy on a shared corpus. Disrobe also disassembles legacy CPython 1.0-2.7. Numeric versions encode as 3 + minor/100 so labels remain ordered.

tools.name: disrobe
tools.source: README.md and xtask/data/recovery.json: CPython 1.0-3.15 dispatch, normalized opcode-structure comparison for the CPython 3.14.5 corpora, and legacy recompile or structural-token checks

tools.name: uncompyle6
tools.source: https://github.com/rocky/python-uncompyle6: CPython 3.0-3.8 bytecode; repository is not archived

tools.name: pycdc

segments.label: broad but partial, no version guarantee

tools.source: zrax/pycdc README: aims at all versions, no per-version correctness guarantee

tools.name: pychd
tools.source: https://github.com/diohabara/pychd: CPython 3.0-3.14; offline deterministic rules recover declarations and common bodies, with unrecovered bodies left as pass; optional LLM assistance fills remaining bodies

footnote: Version support does not establish recovery accuracy or benchmark independence. pychd offers deterministic offline rules and optional LLM assistance; its reported hybrid results include a contamination caveat. Disrobe uses in-tree recovery rules. No shared-corpus accuracy comparison is shown.
